what: Live sandbox-substrate benchmark for the browser-node edge-function runtime (bn-research-js-sandbox-choice measurement half)
browser: Chrome 150.0.0.0 macOS, gm browser verb, page served from 127.0.0.1:3777
method: scratchpad/sandbox-bench/index.html - sandboxed iframe (allow-scripts, NO allow-same-origin, srcdoc guest, postMessage protocol) vs quickjs-emscripten@0.31.0 (esm.sh)

iframe.isolation_witnessed: origin=null (opaque), parent DOM + localStorage + document.cookie all blocked:SecurityError
iframe.not_measured: infinite-loop termination (needs iframe.remove() or worker-in-iframe; no in-place interrupt exists), no memory cap exists

reading: QuickJS is the only substrate with witnessed hard limits (interrupt + memory cap) - required for hostile multi-tenant functions; per-instance boot is 68x cheaper than iframe (1.8ms vs 122.9ms) once the one-time wasm init is paid. Iframe V8 is 11.7x faster on compute (56.2 vs 657.1ms) with native web APIs but offers no in-place interrupt and no memory cap - only whole-iframe teardown. Suggests: QuickJS primary for untrusted functions, iframe as opt-in fast lane for first-party/trusted code. Final call belongs to bn-synthesis-proposal merged with the workflow's published-source research.
